title: Owl Pellet Dissection

title: Face Value: Celebrity Press Photography
tagline: Exploring the evolution of celebrity photography
description: A MoMA exhibition of over 200 studio portraits from 1921–1996 that shows how Hollywood photos were shaped and edited before digital media. It’s family-friendly and free for ages 16 and under, so kids can spot familiar faces like Elizabeth Taylor and Oprah while comparing lighting, makeup, and retouching. Children will come away noticing how photos create a public image.
description_source: The first major exhibition of Hollywood studio portraiture from the Museum’s film stills archive since 1993. Features over 200 works from 1921 to 1996, examining how photographic portraits were manipulated for public consumption before digital technology and social media reshaped celebrity culture. title: Video Games: The Great Connector
tagline: Explore how video games connect and empower youth through play!
description: At the Long Island Museum, this free exhibition has 10 hands-on gaming stations where kids (ages 5–17) can play cooperative and puzzle games. Children can try basic game design, hear stories of Black and Latinx creators, and see Long Island history like 1959’s Tennis for Two. It’s a playful way to practice teamwork and problem-solving; registration is needed for the curator tour.
description_source: This exhibition explores how video games serve as tools for developing teamwork, problem-solving, and social networks among youth. It features 10 interactive gaming stations and highlights contributions by Long Islanders to video game history, including the 1958 creation of Tennis for Two at Brookhaven National Laboratory and the founding of Acclaim Entertainment in Oyster Bay.
